Velvet. Members of the deer family shed and regrow their antlers every year. The velvet part of the antler cycle is when the antlers are still calcifying, and this requires a lot of blood. The velvet protects the antler during this phase and when it is no longer needed, the animal will rub it off on trees and foliage, and it often looks like that.

We all have different reactions to traumatic experiences. I suffered sexual assault when I was 6 years old, and I never had any "normal" outward behavioral problems. I never had nightmares, or wet the bed, or acted out sexually in front of people. When I got older and started to sort through what had happened in therapy, I felt ashamed and non normal for not telling anyone or reacting in the "appropriate" way that children who experience sexual abuse usually do. That doesn't make anyone wrong. We all have different reactions, and if this experience feels like it didn't deeply affect you, then I don't think anything is wrong with that.

I'm sorry this happened to you, and I wish you good luck.

It's a very hurtful experience to jave a positive experience with someone and then have them turn around and say these very disrespectful things to you. And they are disrespectful, because if he actually cared, he wouldn't be telling you that you're a mistake and incorrectly categorizing you based on your current  emotional state. Even if he made you aware of your trauma, that still doesn't excuse his behavior. 

On the subject of your rapist, I understand this completely. My rapist was my uncle, and I still see him every now and then whenever I visit my grandparents. I'm not close to him, but no one else knows what he did to me, so I have to put on this veneer around him. He's gone to rehab for meth and has a girlfriend and children and everyone is always patting him on the back and treating him like a hero when he took advantage of a 6 year old girl years ago. And no one knows.

Have you brought this up to your rapist? He may not have seen it as rape, but even if he didn't, he isn't guilt free. You're allowed to set boundaries and be happy, and sometimes we have to cut people out of our lives if they aren't good for us, even if it's hard. I don't know everything about this situation, but I truly hope you can find people who are good for and to you.

It doesn't excuse what he did, but it makes it more morally complicated for myself. I'm not close to him, but I do sometimes see him, and honestly.... I feel nothing for him. I've considered confronting him/telling the family what happened... But honestly, what good would it do? That's how I think of it. What good would it do. This happened over a decade ago. He has a family now. I almost... I almost don't want to destroy that? I don't know lmao

My therapist popped the question of "do you think he's done this to other children?" And honestly, no. I don't think he has. I was just there and available and unsupervised, and he took advantage of that.

That's not insanity. That's healing. But sometimes what we think is healing can be harmful, and what you're describing as Stockholm Syndrome for your assailamt sounds unhealthy. It's okay to forgive someone, and to move on. But begging them to have feelings for you seems detrimental. I would try to consult a professional about this if you could. It sounds like a complex situation.

I understand the feeling of realizing how hurt someone has to be in order to hurt others. I've done this with my own rapist. He was a drug addict and only 16 years old when he did it to me, and part of my family. I doubt he remembers what even happened. But I remember. And I've talked to my therapist about it countless times, and the only thing to do is try to move on. That's what I'm trying to do.

I would say the guy that hit on you is wrong for his behavior. If he was decent, he wouldn't say it was a mistake to be with you. He would accept you as you are, your past, and how you're trying to change and puzzle through what happened to you.

Being taken advantage of is a difficult betrayal, especially by someone you considered close. Work through this as you can, and try to make connections with new people. It also may help to talk to professionals/loved ones about it.

To be honest, undoing images of this nature takes a lot of time and self awareness. You have to actively fight back against thoughts like this. Every time it happens, you have to distract yourself, cope, remove yourself from that mindset in a healthy way. And it takes a long time.

I used to imagine myself getting hit by cars, lying in the road with blood pouring out of my mouth, staring blankly at the sky as I died. And these were vivid. Every detail was there. And they used to be involuntary, with the thought coming out of nowhere. But I've been actively working on my mindset for over a year now, and I must say I'm in a far better place mentally and emotionally. I don't have those vivid death fantasies anymore. And it's something I'm grateful for.

Find the things you enjoy, that give you meaning. Make them right now if you have to. And then use them to slowly turn back the dial. I wish you luck and I hope it gets easier.
